Decoder of Ogg Opus (plan item P18-07, FEATURE_MATRIX AUD-08), a pure Java implementation of RFC 6716 (the SILK, CELT and hybrid modes with all frame sizes from 2.5 to 60 ms, the four frame packing codes, mono and stereo, redundancy frames, packet loss concealment) and of the Ogg encapsulation of RFC 7845 (header packets, pre-skip, output gain, channel mapping families 0 and 1 with up to eight channels, chained streams, trimming of the last page).

OpusInOgg - Class in org.duckdns.hjow.swingwebpanel.media.audio.opus
Wraps the Opus track of a WebM/Matroska file into an Ogg Opus stream so that the Ogg Opus decoder can play it: the CodecPrivate of the track is the identification header (OpusHead, RFC 7845 section 5.1; it is rebuilt from the track channels and the CodecDelay if it is missing or damaged), every block is one audio packet, and the granule positions of the pages count the decoded samples, with the DiscardPadding of the last block trimmed from the end.

Markdown to HTML conversion for the text/markdown content type (plan items P17-03, P17-04): a self-written block and inline parser that follows CommonMark 0.31.2 (https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/) with the GitHub Flavored Markdown extensions (tables, strikethrough, task lists, extended autolinks, tag filter) behind a switch.
org.duckdns.hjow.swingwebpanel.content.text - package org.duckdns.hjow.swingwebpanel.content.text

WebAnimationHost - Interface in org.duckdns.hjow.swingwebpanel.css.anim
What the Web Animations model needs from the script side of a page (Web Animations Level 1): promises for the ready and finished attributes of the animations, microtasks for the "finish notification steps", and a new animation frame (a call of WebAnimationSet.update(double) followed by a microtask checkpoint and the dispatch of WebAnimationSet.takeEvents()) whenever something waits for one.

The script interface of Web Animations Level 1 (W3C Working Draft 5 June 2023, https://www.w3.org/TR/2023/WD-web-animations-1-20230605/, plan item P10-08-h): Animation (constructor, id, effect, timeline, startTime, currentTime, playbackRate, playState, replaceState, pending, ready, finished, onfinish, oncancel, onremove, play(), pause(), reverse(), finish(), cancel(), updatePlaybackRate(), persist(), commitStyles()), AnimationEffect (getTiming(), getComputedTiming(), updateTiming()), KeyframeEffect (both constructors, target, pseudoElement, composite, iterationComposite of Level 2 which is stored only, getKeyframes(), setKeyframes()), AnimationTimeline and DocumentTimeline (constructor with originTime), AnimationPlaybackEvent, Element.animate(), Element.getAnimations({subtree}), Document.getAnimations() and document.timeline.

The Web Animations state of one document (Web Animations Level 1): the animations created by scripts in their global order (the composite order among them), the time of the document that the WebTimelines follow, the pending animation event queue and the procedure "update animations and send events" (WebAnimationSet.update(double) for the timelines, the pending tasks, the finished states and the removal of replaced animations, then WebAnimationSet.takeEvents() after the host's microtask checkpoint).

WebResponse - Class in org.duckdns.hjow.swingwebpanel.js.host
The result of a WebRequest, already filtered by the component's network policy the way the Fetch Standard filters responses: a basic response (same origin, without Set-Cookie), a cors response (cross origin that the server allowed, with only the safelisted and the exposed headers), an opaque response (cross origin no-cors: status 0, no headers, no body) or an error response (network error: refused by CORS or by the scheme policy, blocked redirect, failed connection, cancelled request).

The XML serialization of a DOM node, as defined for XMLSerializer (W3C DOM Parsing and Serialization, "XML Serialization", with the require well-formed flag unset): elements and attributes are written so that their namespaces are kept, with prefixes and namespace declarations added, replaced or dropped as needed (xmlns and xmlns:prefix are generated where a namespace has no usable prefix; ns1, ns2 ... are generated prefixes); an HTML element without children is written with a start and end tag, except the void elements, which are written as <br />; elements of other namespaces without children are written as <a/>; text escapes & < >, attribute values also escape the quotation mark, tab, line feed and carriage return.
